images.caption: Figure 1:Avatar referring segmentation withHumanSkill-4D.(a)A 3D query selects the described region of a Gaussian avatar (Where).(b)A 4D query also selects the intervals in which the specified pose or motion occurs (When). See ourproject pagefor video demos.

Figure 2:HumanSkill-4Doverview.(Offline)We build a semantic memory for each avatar, a motion memory for its driving pose sequence, and an operator registry shared across avatars.(Online)The frozen MLLM selects target categories from their names and descriptions, and their stored scores determine the spatial mask. For a 4D query, it also reads the registry’s text cards and composes operators into a motion program, and running the program on the joint trajectories gives the temporal mask. The two masks give the spatiotemporal selection. In this example, the program identifies intervals when both upper arms move outward, andStateAtEndretains each movement interval whose last frame has both arms horizontal (orange band).
